lines.text: One, three, six, ten, fifteen. Each step adds one more than the last.
lines.caption: One, three, six, ten, fifteen. Each step adds one more than the last.

lines.text: Go on for one hundred numbers. How many are multiples of three? <short pause> A neat pattern is hiding here.
lines.caption: Go on for one hundred numbers. How many are multiples of three? A neat pattern is hiding here.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this one together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this one together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: So the list goes one, three, six, ten, fifteen, and it keeps going.
lines.caption: So the list goes one, three, six, ten, fifteen, and it keeps going.

lines.text: How many of the first one hundred numbers in the list are multiples of three?
lines.caption: How many of the first one hundred numbers in the list are multiples of three?

lines.text: Is it thirty-three, thirty-four, fifty, sixty-six, or sixty-seven?
lines.caption: Is it thirty-three, thirty-four, fifty, sixty-six, or sixty-seven?

lines.text: Let's number the spots. Spot one holds one, spot two holds three, spot three holds six.
lines.caption: Let's number the spots. Spot one holds one, spot two holds three, spot three holds six.

lines.text: We need to count the spots, from one to one hundred, that hold a multiple of three.
lines.caption: We need to count the spots, from one to one hundred, that hold a multiple of three.

lines.text: The last number is over five thousand. Too big to list them all! We need a pattern.
lines.caption: The last number is over five thousand. Too big to list them all! We need a pattern.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our strategy: forget the big numbers. Track the remainder when you divide by three.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our strategy: forget the big numbers. Track the remainder when you divide by three.

lines.text: One leaves a remainder of one. Three leaves zero, so it's a multiple.
lines.caption: One leaves a remainder of one. Three leaves zero, so it's a multiple.

lines.text: Each number is the one before, plus a bit more. So we can just add up the remainders!
lines.caption: Each number is the one before, plus a bit more. So we can just add up the remainders!

lines.text: Six is three plus three. Adding a three never changes the remainder. So six leaves zero.
lines.caption: Six is three plus three. Adding a three never changes the remainder. So six leaves zero.

lines.text: Ten is six plus four. Four leaves one. Zero plus one is one, so ten leaves one.
lines.caption: Ten is six plus four. Four leaves one. Zero plus one is one, so ten leaves one.

lines.text: Fifteen is ten plus five. Five leaves two. One plus two is three, which leaves zero!
lines.caption: Fifteen is ten plus five. Five leaves two. One plus two is three, which leaves zero!

lines.text: Twenty-one is fifteen plus six. Adding six changes nothing, so it leaves zero.
lines.caption: Twenty-one is fifteen plus six. Adding six changes nothing, so it leaves zero.

lines.text: See the pattern? One, zero, zero. Then one, zero, zero again.
lines.caption: See the pattern? One, zero, zero. Then one, zero, zero again.

lines.text: Why does it keep repeating? Every three steps, we add three numbers in a row.
lines.caption: Why does it keep repeating? Every three steps, we add three numbers in a row.

lines.text: Like four, five and six. Together they make fifteen, which is five threes.
lines.caption: Like four, five and six. Together they make fifteen, which is five threes.

lines.text: Three numbers in a row always make a multiple of three. So the remainder comes right back.
lines.caption: Three numbers in a row always make a multiple of three. So the remainder comes right back.

lines.text: So the list comes in groups of three spots. The remainders go one, zero, zero.
lines.caption: So the list comes in groups of three spots. The remainders go one, zero, zero.

lines.text: Every group holds exactly two multiples of three, in its second and third spots.
lines.caption: Every group holds exactly two multiples of three, in its second and third spots.

lines.text: One hundred is thirty-three threes, plus one. That's thirty-three full groups, and one extra spot.
lines.caption: One hundred is thirty-three threes, plus one. That's thirty-three full groups, and one extra spot.

lines.text: Thirty-three groups, times two each, gives sixty-six multiples.
lines.caption: Thirty-three groups, times two each, gives sixty-six multiples.

lines.text: The extra spot is spot one hundred. It starts a new group, so it leaves one. Not a multiple!
lines.caption: The extra spot is spot one hundred. It starts a new group, so it leaves one. Not a multiple!

lines.text: So the answer is sixty-six. That's D!
lines.caption: So the answer is sixty-six. That's D!

lines.text: Here's a second way. Each number is a sum. Spot four holds one plus two plus three plus four.
lines.caption: Here's a second way. Each number is a sum. Spot four holds one plus two plus three plus four.

lines.text: Draw it as a staircase of dots. Then add a second copy, flipped upside down.
lines.caption: Draw it as a staircase of dots. Then add a second copy, flipped upside down.

lines.text: Together they make a rectangle, four by five. That's twenty dots, so one staircase is ten.
lines.caption: Together they make a rectangle, four by five. That's twenty dots, so one staircase is ten.

lines.text: The same works for any spot. Spot n holds n times n plus one, all divided by two.
lines.caption: The same works for any spot. Spot n holds n times n plus one, all divided by two.

lines.text: When is that a multiple of three? The top, n times n plus one, is twice our number.
lines.caption: When is that a multiple of three? The top, n times n plus one, is twice our number.

lines.text: Twice a number is a multiple of three exactly when the number is. So let's just check the top.
lines.caption: Twice a number is a multiple of three exactly when the number is. So let's just check the top.

lines.text: Two whole numbers multiply to a multiple of three only when one of them is a multiple of three.
lines.caption: Two whole numbers multiply to a multiple of three only when one of them is a multiple of three.

lines.text: First, n itself: three, six, up to ninety-nine. That's thirty-three spots.
lines.caption: First, n itself: three, six, up to ninety-nine. That's thirty-three spots.

lines.text: Next, n plus one: n is two, five, up to ninety-eight. That's thirty-three more.
lines.caption: Next, n plus one: n is two, five, up to ninety-eight. That's thirty-three more.

lines.text: Neighbors can't both be multiples of three. So it's thirty-three plus thirty-three: sixty-six again!
lines.caption: Neighbors can't both be multiples of three. So it's thirty-three plus thirty-three: sixty-six again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you know the formula, it gives the rule for every spot at once.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When you know the formula, it gives the rule for every spot at once.

lines.text: Thirty-three counts only spots three, six, nine, and so on. It forgets spots like two, five and eight.
lines.caption: Thirty-three counts only spots three, six, nine, and so on. It forgets spots like two, five and eight.

lines.text: Thirty-four is what you'd get counting spots one, four, seven, up to one hundred. They all leave one!
lines.caption: Thirty-four is what you'd get counting spots one, four, seven, up to one hundred. They all leave one!

lines.text: Fifty is what you'd get guessing every other number. But the pattern repeats every three, not two.
lines.caption: Fifty is what you'd get guessing every other number. But the pattern repeats every three, not two.

lines.text: Sixty-seven is what you'd get if you counted the extra spot too. But spot one hundred leaves one.
lines.caption: Sixty-seven is what you'd get if you counted the extra spot too. But spot one hundred leaves one.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Find the cycle, count the full groups, then check the leftovers one by one.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Find the cycle, count the full groups, then check the leftovers one by one.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same list, but now take just the first eighty numbers.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same list, but now take just the first eighty numbers.

lines.text: How many of them are multiples of three? Use the same plan. Groups of three first!
lines.caption: How many of them are multiples of three? Use the same plan. Groups of three first!

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Eighty is twenty-six threes, plus two. So, twenty-six full groups and two extra spots.
lines.caption: Let's check. Eighty is twenty-six threes, plus two. So, twenty-six full groups and two extra spots.

lines.text: Twenty-six groups, times two each, gives fifty-two multiples.
lines.caption: Twenty-six groups, times two each, gives fifty-two multiples.

lines.text: The two extra spots leave one, then zero. That's one more! Fifty-two plus one is fifty-three.
lines.caption: The two extra spots leave one, then zero. That's one more! Fifty-two plus one is fifty-three.

lines.text: Formula check: twenty-six spots for n, and twenty-seven for n plus one. Fifty-three again!
lines.caption: Formula check: twenty-six spots for n, and twenty-seven for n plus one. Fifty-three again!

lines.text: If you found fifty-three, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found fifty-three, amazing work!

lines.text: Don't chase the big numbers. Track the remainders, and find the rule for which spots work.
lines.caption: Don't chase the big numbers. Track the remainders, and find the rule for which spots work.

lines.text: The pattern is one, zero, zero. So in every full group of three spots, two are multiples.
lines.caption: The pattern is one, zero, zero. So in every full group of three spots, two are multiples.
